newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Sendzimir steel mill readies for sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Polish Sendzimir steel mill readies for sell-off.

text.p: Poland's largest steel mill, Huta im. Sendzimira SA, is likely to be privatised by the end of the year, the company's director general said on Tuesday.
Jerzy Knapik told reporters that by the end of April three daughter companies should be carved out from Sendzimir and later separately privatised through sales of new shares to strategic investors.
"Three companies -- the steel mill, power house and mechanical works -- should be carved out and undergo privatisation," he said.
He said six investors were interested in buying a stake in Sendzimir's steel mill, three in purchasing the power house's shares and one in the mechanical works.
Knapik said he would like the Sendzimir parent company, owned by the state, to retain 51-percent stakes in the three firms.
"But this may prove difficult because investors may not want to provide financing and technologies if they do not have a majority stake," he said.
He said Sendzimir's steel mill itself needed $200 million in investment to face foreign competition after Poland lifts barriers protecting its steel sector in the next several years.
He said three bidders for the mill would be shorlisted by end of June.
Last year, the then deputy treasury minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said large listed Western and Japanese companies were interested in Sendzimir.
Sendzimir, based near the southern city of Krakow, saw its net profit fall to estimated 18-20 million zlotys last year from 100 million in 1995 due to harsh winter and bad climate in steel industry.
The company had sales of 2.9 billion zlotys in 1996.
